solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sudden realisation: holiday finished

parts.note: a break is a short holiday, as in a city break
through means done or finished, as in 'I'm through with it'

explanation.surface: Someone on the last day of a trip suddenly sees things clearly.
explanation.definitionFit: A discovery that suddenly solves a problem, the moment an idea finally clicks, is a sudden realisation.

clue.text: Operated trial venue — no time for spite

parts.note: ran means operated, as in ran a business

indicators.note: no means the letter for time is left out

parts.note: a court is where a trial is held

explanation.surface: A courtroom run with no time to spare breeds ill will.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is bitter, long-lasting resentment, close in meaning to spite or malice.

clue.text: COs play recklessly with weapon in war film

indicators.note: recklessly signals letters thrown about without care, so the given letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Commanding officers fool around carelessly with a gun on a movie set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'COs' are commanding officers, but here just letters; 'play' looks like the verb but is also fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Francis Ford Coppola's 1979 film set in the Vietnam War, a classic war film.

clue.text: Left during closing parts of latest contemporary score

indicators.note: during puts the word for left within the two closing letters
closing parts are the last letters of each of the two words

parts.note: went means left, as in departed

explanation.surface: Someone walked out during the end of a modern musical score.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letters of latest and contemporary are T and Y; WENT goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is a set of twenty, an old counting word as in threescore years and ten.

clue.text: Respond to provocation online, as it were?

definitions.meaning: to react angrily to a deliberate taunt
a fish that comes up to take the bait ends up on the angler's line, so it is jokingly 'online'

explanation.surface: Someone is warned about how to react to trolls on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Online' suggests the internet, but the second reading is a hooked fish on a fishing line.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish rises to the surface to take a lure, and people do the same when they react to a taunt.

clue.text: Customary behaviour in the American era?

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for American, from United States
an age is an era

explanation.surface: A question about the typical habits of the American period.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage means habitual practice or custom, the established way things are done.

clue.text: Rustic, say, rambling, gathering attention round

indicators.note: gathering means taking in, so the word for attention holds the shuffled letters

parts.note: heed means attention, as in pay heed

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about, so the three letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A country type talks on and on, drawing everyone's notice around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambling' is the anagram signal and 'gathering' puts that inside the word for attention; 'round' simply reinforces the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Hayseed is informal, chiefly American, slang for an unsophisticated country person, a rustic or yokel.

clue.text: Second taxi delivering strike-breaker

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A second taxi driver ferries in workers who cross the picket line.
explanation.definitionFit: Scab is a derogatory term for a worker who keeps working during a strike, a blackleg.

clue.text: Very motivated to list first pair of comets

indicators.note: to list two items is to set them out with a joining word between, so the conjunction sits between the two letters
first pair of picks the opening two letters of the word comets

parts.note: to joins one item to the next, the way and does in a list

explanation.surface: An astronomer is keen to catalogue a couple of comets.
explanation.walkthrough: Together 'to list' means set out the two letters as a list, C and O, with the joining word between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A can-do attitude is eager, energetic and confident about getting things done, so it describes someone very motivated.

clue.text: City to remain in receipt of second great joy

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London

indicators.note: something in receipt of another holds it, so the word for remain takes the letter for second inside it

parts.note: to stay is to remain

explanation.surface: A city worker is delighted to be kept on after receiving a second payment.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy is an overwhelming feeling of happiness, a synonym for rapture or great joy.

clue.text: Happy solver taken aback, beset by black insect

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the reversed word sits between the letter for black and the insect

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an ant is an insect

indicators.note: taken aback is read literally as turned back, so the word for solver is written backwards

parts.note: the solver is addressed as you

explanation.surface: A cheerful solver is startled when a little black bug crawls over them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken aback' reverses the solver's pronoun, and 'beset by' surrounds it with the colour letter and the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Buoyant means cheerful and optimistic, in high spirits, as well as able to float.

clue.text: Those people having little energy for the topic

parts.note: them is the pronoun for those people
E is the abbreviation for energy, so a little of it is just that letter

explanation.surface: A group with little energy has to settle on the subject of discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject a talk or piece of writing is about, so it is a topic.

clue.text: One suffering pretentious visiting mister!

indicators.note: visiting puts one thing within another, so the word for pretentious sits inside the abbreviation for mister

parts.note: arty can mean affectedly artistic, pretentious

explanation.surface: Someone has to endure a visit from a pompous gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A martyr is a person who suffers or dies for a belief, or who makes a show of suffering.

clue.text: Takes care of alien way of thinking

parts.note: minds means looks after, takes care of
ET is the alien from the Spielberg film E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial

explanation.surface: Someone looks after a visitor from outer space with an unusual outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: A mindset is a person's habitual attitude or outlook, a fixed way of thinking.

clue.text: I had to follow many round, showing little emotion

indicators.note: to follow puts the contraction after the other piece
round means turned about, so the word for many is read backwards

parts.note: lots means many
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone must trail a crowd around, keeping a blank expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' reverses the word for many, and 'to follow' puts the contraction after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stolid person is calm, dependable and shows little feeling or excitement, impassive.

clue.text: Generous representation of Braille

indicators.note: a representation of a word recasts it in a new form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A generous transcription into the raised-dot script for the blind.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal can mean given freely and in large amounts, as in a liberal helping, so lavish or generous.

clue.text: Church aisle reshaped without a woodworking tool

indicators.note: reshaped asks for a rearrangement, and without says the a is subtracted from the word's letters

explanation.surface: A church's walkway has been remodelled without carpentry gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reshaped without a' means drop one A from the word aisle and rearrange the four letters left, after the church abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A chisel is a bladed hand tool used with a mallet for shaping wood, a woodworking tool.

clue.text: Calls sailor over after first article's dropped

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the remaining letters are read backwards
dropped means that letter is taken out of the word for sailor

parts.note: a seaman is a sailor

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word article, which is also the first article of grammar

explanation.surface: Someone shouts for a sailor to come over once the first item has been delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: SEAMAN loses its first A to give SEMAN, and 'over' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: To call someone something is to give them that title, as a verb meaning to label or designate.

clue.text: Type of computer peripheral lines available in 2000

indicators.note: available in puts the poem inside the Roman number

parts.note: MM is 2000 in Roman numerals
an ode is a poem, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A kind of computer add-on first went on sale at the turn of the millennium.
explanation.definitionFit: A modem is a device connected to a computer for sending data over phone lines, an external peripheral.

clue.text: Scoundrel going to pub and cobblers

parts.note: a heel is a contemptible person, a scoundrel
a bar is a pub or drinking place

explanation.surface: A rogue heads to the pub, and that is all rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cobblers' looks like British slang for nonsense; here it means shoe-repairers. A heel bar is a small shop or kiosk mending shoes while you wait.
explanation.definitionFit: A heel bar is a place where shoes are repaired, a cobbler's shop, so it stands for cobblers.

clue.text: Regret about daughter showing bad manners

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for regret goes round the letter for daughter

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A parent regrets how impolite their daughter has been.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude means impolite or discourteous, displaying poor manners.

clue.text: Part of marshalling yard, Southern, is to suppress noise — good

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down or contain, so is closes around the noise and the good

parts.note: din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A railway worker in the south is told to keep the noise down: a good thing.
explanation.walkthrough: A marshalling yard is where railway wagons are sorted into trains; the side tracks there are sidings.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidings are short stretches of track off the main line where wagons are parked, a large part of any marshalling yard.

clue.text: Sharp and tart? That's about right

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for tart surrounds the letter for right

parts.note: acid means sour or tart in taste

explanation.surface: Someone tastes something and pronounces it sharp and sour, and is told that is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid means unpleasantly sharp or pungent in taste or smell, so it matches sharp.

clue.text: Famous archer, familiarly, after period in prison? We'll see

indicators.note: after places the archer's name behind the prison term

parts.note: time is slang for a prison sentence, as in doing time
William Tell, the legendary Swiss archer, gets the familiar short form of his first name

explanation.surface: A celebrated archer, released after a stretch inside, wonders what comes next.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the future will reveal the outcome, an idiom equivalent to saying we shall find out later.
